key_points: Only WFC-specific signal is the $50B 2026 NII target, framed as driven by loan growth, deposit growth, fixed-rate asset repricing and balance-sheet expansion; reads as a reaffirmation of an existing recovery thesis rather than new information, so impact is low-to-moderate.

A contrarian note that WFC still missed on interest income keeps the NII optimism from being fully confirmed; treat the $50B figure as a target to be validated by actual reported NII, not as delivered results.
Preferred-stock selloff and 8% yields piece is sector income commentary with only indirect read-across (WFC as an issuer); not thesis-changing for the common equity.
Headlines on Nvidia/Jensen Huang, credit-card phone protection, HeartFlow fair value, PNC peer performance and DraftKings are noise for WFC and should carry zero weight.
Net: modestly positive tone but low actionable content; wait for Q4 print and 2026 guidance detail on NII, expenses and credit before adjusting position size.
